office_does: An Okanogan County PUD commissioner sits on the three-member elected board that sets rates, the budget and policy for the public electric and wholesale broadband utility; the seat is nominated by district and elected by the whole PUD for six years.
race_blurb: Incumbent Scott Vejraska, an 11-year commissioner, board president and lineman, runs on rate restraint; assistant state auditor Steven Gadd, a former Okanogan City Council member, says twelve years is long enough and promises closer oversight. Nonpartisan.

candidates.summary: Okanogan County PUD commissioner for 11 years and current board president, a lineman for 27 years and a rancher.
highlights: Says he has opposed unnecessary rate increases 'with a firm NO VOTE, whenever possible' [S1]
Says reserves were strengthened after wildfire damage without added burden on ratepayers [S1]

candidates.summary: Assistant state auditor for 14 years and former Okanogan City Council member, with an MBA and management-accounting certifications.
highlights: 'It's time for a change. Twelve years is long enough in any elected position!' [S1]
Promises 'thorough oversite' and openness to public and employee input [S1]
Served four years on the Okanogan City Council [S1]
